script.base: Closed-roof home favorite Arizona (implied 26.2) leads by halftime in a moderate 45.5 game, not a shootout and not a slog. Murray feeds McBride (week-1 team-high 9 targets, 35 air yards) in the middle early, then the lead back James Conner (12 carries week 1) closes. Carolina, a 7-point dog implied at 19.2, throws more once behind; pace stays ordinary.

Run overlap is Conner (12 carries, lead back) into the 6.73 YPC CAR front missing Wharton; Benson's 8/69 is the same front but the line already prices the explosion.

pre_mortem: It's Monday and both overs lost. Conner stayed at 12 carries or fewer because Benson again took the efficient work (week 1 was 8/69 vs 12/39) and Murray kept a 7-carry, 38-yard share, Hernandez sat with the knee, and Carolina's 6.73 YPC was one-game noise against a different offense. McBride never saw a second 9-target day: ARI led by two scores at half, closed with Conner, and the middle 9.25 YPA was eight throws that CAR took away. Both lines were just week-1 medians plus a half point, and with no anchor price there was never proof the number was wrong. That counter is why McBride is only a lean and why Conner is flagged rather than sized. It is not stronger than Wharton-out plus 6.73 YPC plus a 39.5 lead-back line, so Conner stays.
slip_story: One story: Arizona's offense in a home lead, not a shootout stack and not a game under. Conner rush over is the weak-front closer leg. McBride rec over is the same offense attacking CAR's middle before any kill-clock. They win together if ARI scores near 26 without a first-quarter blowout. Do not add Benson rush over (that needs the carries Conner is taking) or McMillan rec over (needs CAR to convert deep air into a defense that allowed 1 of 45 explosives, the opposite efficiency read). Hubbard rush under would fit the dog-trails flip but was left off the two-player cap. No TDs, no second market on either player.
